longForm.overview:
Teacher is the emoji of role-coded profession reveal - the career tradition, the role cue, and the universal "this is my profession" tag. Where 💼 reads as briefcase-coded work energy and 🧑 reads as person-coded identity energy, Teacher captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate role-coded profession energy - a "teacher" role tag or a career-coded reveal.

The role cue borrows from profession tradition and the modern role-coded aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as role-coded rather than literal.

What separates Teacher from the rest of the role family is the specific teacher register. The emoji is not saying 'generic role' (💼). It is saying 'teacher-coded teacher,' which carries a specific profession, career, or role specificity.

In real-world usage 🧑‍🏫 Teacher lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate role energy. A partner sends it on a "teacher" moment. A friend sends it on a "role" reveal. A coworker sends it on a "teacher" tag. The teacher cue is what makes the emoji feel role-coded - it is not just 'a moment,' it is 'teacher-coded energy.'

In dating 🧑‍🏫 Teacher works as a soft-coded teacher tag, where the teacher cue signals profession. In work threads 🧑‍🏫 Teacher lives as a quick coded check-in. Across all of these surfaces the rule is the same: the more role the moment, the more natural 🧑‍🏫 feels.

longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip Teacher in sympathy, condolence, or break-up contexts. The role-coded profession cue is the wrong register for somber moments. A quiet ❤️ or a sentence that acknowledges the moment is a better fit.

Avoid Teacher in casual contexts where the role energy feels too formal. A simpler emoji or a sentence keeps the message grounded.

Skip Teacher when you want to communicate identity beyond profession. The role register is too career-coded for personal moments; use 🧑 or a sentence when the moment needs the whole person.
